newsitem.title: UK: London clean tanker rates mixed, Med firmer.
newsitem.headline: London clean tanker rates mixed, Med firmer.

text.p: World product tanker rates were a mixed bag this week, with rates for trips to the Far East looking weak while prices in the Mediterranean moved higher, shipbrokers said on Friday.
Mediterranean gas oil tanker rates for 30,000 tonne cargoes were quoted around W215/220 against W200 seen last week.
Naphtha cargoes of approximately 27,000 tonnes were assessed at W235 similar to last week's levels.
"It was a week of great expectations in the Mediterranean with enquiry quickly outstripping suitable available tonnage," said shipbrokers Gibson in their weekly report.
Far East rates were fragile due to a dearth of orders.
"The market is now noticeably two-tier with the better quality tonnage endeavouring to secure naphtha stems to the Far East," commented shipping brokers Galbraith's in their weekly report.

"One owner with a vessel open on May 19 has reportedly fixed off a 3-5 June position in order to secure a naphtha cargo which is paying 15-20 percent higher than what is currently available for gas oil cargoes," Galbraith's said.
For 30,000 tonners on Middle East/India trips rates were assessed around W170/175, while 55,000 tonners doing Middle East/Japan trips were seen commanding around W175.
The inter-UKCont market was fairly active with rates for 25,000 tonnes doing cross sector trips fetching around W205.
There was a fair amount of interest for clean vessels to do Transatlantic trips.

"Interest in lifting clean product from Ventspils or U.K.-continent to the USAC increased throughout the week, with unleaded mogas cargoes of 33,000 tonnes being fixed at approximately W235," Gibson shipbrokers said in their report.
